chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muthannā, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Fasting three days in every month has become difficult for me, so what would suffice for me? That I give charity in place of each day with one dirham?
So he said: “The charity of one dirham is better than fasting one day.”

key_terms.أَتَصَدَّقَ: to give charity, as a substitute act of devotion
key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: better or more virtuous in this context
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: three days, referring to the monthly recommended observance
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a dirham, the specified amount of charity
key_terms.صَوْمُ: fasting, specifically the recommended fast being discussed
key_terms.كُلِّ شَهْرٍ: every month, indicating the regular devotional practice

ai.seo_question: What can a person do if fasting three recommended days every month becomes difficult?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the case of someone who finds the recommended fast of three days each month difficult. Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that giving one dirham in charity for each day is superior to fasting a single day in its place.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1794 - It is narrated by Ibn Muskan from Ibrahim ibn al-Muthanna, who said:
"I said to Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)): 'Fasting three days every month has become difficult for me. What would suffice for me? Can I give charity in place of each day, a dirham?'
Imam (as) said: 'Giving charity of a dirham is better than fasting a day.'"
